summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic anxiety was readmitted shortly after discharge due to nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea after consuming orange juice. She was found to have a UTI caused by coagulase-negative staph, acute kidney injury from dehydration, and a gastroparesis flare possibly complicated by gastroenteritis. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids via a newly placed PICC line, antibiotics, and antiemetics. Her blood pressure was elevated, so lisinopril was increased to 20 mg daily. Insulin therapy was continued with Lantus and sliding scale Humalog. Psychiatry and social work evaluated her anxiety, noting regressive behaviors, and recommended outpatient counseling and possible SSRI restart. She improved over five days, tolerated a full diet, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
